sections.title: Frontend framework settings
sections.what: Turns on React strict mode and passes the backend address into the frontend under one name.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes the backend address available to frontend code in one place.
sections.watch_out: Anything placed here is visible to every visitor's browser, so never put secrets in it.

summary: Settings for the Next.js frontend framework. It turns on extra React checks and sets the backend address the browser uses.
purpose: Tells the frontend build and development server how to behave and which backend to call.
why: Likely reason: strict checks catch React mistakes early, and the default address lets local development work without setup.
how: Exports one settings object. It turns on strict React checks, then passes the backend address from an environment variable. If that variable is missing, it uses localhost port 8000.
inputs: The NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL environment variable, if it is set.
outputs: A settings object that Next.js reads when it starts or builds.
risks: If the variable is missing in a shared or deployed build, the frontend calls localhost, which other users cannot reach. Anything set here is visible in the browser.
debug: If the screens cannot reach the backend, check the address the app uses and the environment variable. Restart after changing it, because Next.js reads it at startup.
